housing.summary: Barcelona has a competitive, high-demand rental market, especially in central districts (Eixample, Ciutat Vella, Gràcia). Furnished and unfurnished flats are common; a deposit plus first month's rent is typically required up front, and many landlords request proof of income or a guarantor. Most searches happen through online portals and local agencies.

banking.summary: Opening a resident bank account generally requires an NIE (foreigner ID number), passport, proof of address, and proof of employment or income. Non-resident accounts are also available with fewer documents. Major Spanish retail banks operate widely across the city with English-language support at larger branches.

schools.summary: Barcelona offers public schools (instruction primarily in Catalan, with Spanish), concertados (state-subsidised private), and a broad range of international schools serving expatriate families. International options include British, American, French, German and International Baccalaureate curricula. Public school placement is tied to residential registration (empadronamiento).

legal_admin.summary: New residents must obtain an NIE and register on the municipal padrón (empadronamiento) at their local district office (Oficina d'Atenció Ciutadana) to prove local residence. The padrón certificate is required for many administrative steps including school enrolment and healthcare registration. EU/EEA citizens register on the Central Register of Foreigners; non-EU nationals require the appropriate residence authorisation.
legal_admin.registration_step: Empadronamiento (municipal residence registration on the padrón)

tax_finance.summary: Individuals need a tax identification number to work and file taxes: Spanish nationals use the NIF, and foreigners use the NIE, which also serves as their tax identifier. Residents are taxed on worldwide income; Spain's national tax authority administers income tax (IRPF), with some devolved competencies at the Catalan regional level.

transport.summary: Barcelona has an extensive integrated public transport network covering metro, buses, trams and local trains, managed under a single fare-integration authority with zone-based ticketing. Rechargeable travel cards cover unlimited travel within a zone for a set period. EU/EEA driving licences are valid; many non-EU licences must be exchanged, and health coverage is accessed by registering for a regional public health card after empadronamiento.
transport.network_name: TMB (Metro & Bus) / ATM integrated fare network
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences valid without exchange; non-EU licences must be exchanged (where a bilateral agreement exists) within 6 months of residency, otherwise a Spanish test is required
transport.healthcare_registration: Register with the Catalan public health service (CatSalut) after empadronamiento to obtain a health card (TSI)
